title: What a Gursikh does
hookLine: Bhai Gurdas pictures the Sikh who rises early, bathes, remembers, joins the sangat and works honestly

lines: A DAY TOLD BY THE CLOCK.
cards: What would a stranger learn about you from watching one ordinary day? Not your opinions. Just the day: what time the light went on, what you did first, where you went, how you earned your bread.
Bhai Gurdas gives us the day of a Sikh who belongs to the Guru, and he doesn't describe it with a list of beliefs. He describes it with a clock. Today's word: Gursikh.

teach.h: GUR AND SIKH: A SIKH OF THE GURU.
teach.b: Gursikh puts two words together: Gur, the Guru, and Sikh. A Sikh of the Guru. Bhai Gurdas returns to this person in his vars, and the picture he paints is practical, almost a timetable.
The Gursikh rises while the night is still on, in the early hours.
Bathes. Then remembers: sits with the Guru's word, with the Name, before the day's noise starts.

Then goes to the sangat, to sit with others and hear and sing the Guru's hymns. Then goes to work, earns a living honestly, and shares what comes in. No mountaintop, no cave: a house, a gathering, a workplace.
The picture has deep roots in the Guru's own word.

On Ang three hundred five of the Guru Granth Sahib, Guru Ram Das describes the one who calls himself a Sikh of the Guru: rising early, bathing, meditating on the Name, and carrying the Guru's word through the rest of the day.
Bhai Gurdas fills in the day around that morning. Three things stand out. First, the order.

Remembering comes before the work, so the work happens inside the remembering, not instead of it. Second, the company. The Gursikh's day isn't solitary: the sangat is part of the schedule, not an extra.
Third, the money. Honest work is in the picture on purpose. Holiness doesn't leave the marketplace; it walks into it with clean hands.

teach.h: KNOWN BY THE SHAPE OF A DAY.
teach.b: A Gursikh, in this telling, isn't known by a title.
You'd know one by watching the day.

how: Sikh custom keeps the amrit vela, the hours before dawn, for bathing and reciting or listening to the morning banis before the day's work.

o: a Sikh born into a family of the Gurus
a Sikh of the Guru, known by the shape of the day
a senior Sikh teacher who leads the gurdwara

games.q: the Gursikh's day — tap the pairs.
p: rise while night is still on

s: Bhai Gurdas's Gursikh leaves work behind to pray
honest work is part of the Gursikh's day in his picture.

games.q: you want to live as a Sikh of the Guru. where does your day start?
o: at work, as early as possible.
rising early, bathing, and remembering the Name.
late, after a long night of reading.
games.why: Guru Ram Das (Ang 305) starts the Sikh's day early: rising, bathing, remembering the Name. Bhai Gurdas adds the sangat and honest work around it.

practice: Picture tomorrow's first ten or fifteen minutes, a little before your usual alarm, while the house is still quiet.
See what you'd do with them before the phone, wash your face, sit, breathe, read a line that matters to you, and keep it small enough to be real.
If you pray, you can choose a line of the Guru's word, or say Waheguru, for that quiet.

wordCard.voice: Gursikh. A Sikh of the Guru. In Bhai Gurdas's vars, someone you'd recognize by the day: rising early, remembering, sitting in the sangat, working honestly.

orig.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi: a Sikh of the Guru, from gur and sikh.

carryVoice: Your line: the gursikh's day. Remembering first, and the work held inside it. Until tomorrow.
